# odyssey-082 — new recurring renderings (17.1–100)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἄλκιμον ἔγχος (17.4) | "a sturdy spear" | "his sturdy spear" | "strong spear" (the table fixes "sturdy" at 15.551 and odyssey-076 ships it for this same half-line), "valiant", "stout" (kept for στιβαρός), "mighty"; not new: follows the table row |
| συβώτης (17.5) | "swineherd" | "swineherd" | "herdsman", "pig-keeper"; the same man is ὑφορβός elsewhere and is "swineherd" there too |
| ἄττα (vocative, 17.6) | "Father" | "Father" | "Daddy", "Old man" (reserved for ὦ γέρον), "Sir"; courteous address to an older man, no family tie (unlike πάτερ ὦ ξεῖνε and ὦ πάτερ) |
| ὦ φίλος (vocative, 17.17) | "O friend" | "Friend" | "O dear one", "my friend" in `i`, "dear sir", "good fellow"; follows the table row ὦ φίλος (nominative as vocative); ξεῖνε φίλε stays "Dear stranger" |
| πτωχός · πτωχεύω · δαῖτα πτωχεύειν (17.11, 17.18–19) | "beggar" · "to beg" · "a meal to beg" | "beggar" · "beg" · "beg a meal" | "mendicant", "tramp", "ask for alms", "wander begging" |
| πύρνον καὶ κοτύλην (17.12) | "a wheaten loaf and a cup" | "a wheaten loaf and a cup" | "wheat-bread", "a loaf and a drink", "bread and a mug", "a cupful of wine" (the Greek names no wine); follows the table row κοτύλη · πύρνος (15.312) |
| ἄλγιον (17.14) | "more painful" | "the more painful" | "worse", "more bitter"; the comparative of the word in ἄλγεα "pains" |
| σταθμός (17.20, 17.26 farm; 17.96 post) | "steading" (of the farm) · "post" (of the hall) | "steading" (of the farm) · "post of the hall" | "farm" in `i` (kept for ἀγρός), "stable", "doorway", "pillar" as if certain; follows the table row σταθμός (14.358) "a steading" / "the steading"; the same noun in both senses, note says so |
| σημάντωρ (17.21) | "overseer" | "overseer" | "master", "commander", "herald" |
| ἀνὴρ ὅδε (17.22) | "this man here" | "this man here" | "this fellow", "this man" alone (drops ὅδε) |
| δόμους εὖ ναιετάοντας (17.28, 17.85) | "the well-inhabited house" | "the well-inhabited house" | "the well-built house" (that is εὖ ναιετάοντας read as 'well-placed', unknown), "the fair dwelling", "the comfortable homes"; the plural δόμους is said to be a plural for one dwelling in the note |
| δαιδαλέος (17.32, of chairs) | "wrought" | "finely wrought" | "cunningly wrought", "intricate" (reserved for ποικίλος δεσμός), "ornate"; follows the shipped "the much-wrought chamber" for πολυδαίδαλον |
| κώεα (17.32) | "fleeces" | "fleeces" | "rugs", "sheepskins", "coverings" |
| κλισμός (17.86, 17.90, 17.97) | "seat" | "seat" | "couch", "stool", "easy-chair", "reclining chair"; θρόνος stays "chair", and κλισμῷ κεκλιμένη keeps the shared root in the note |
| ἠλάκατα (17.97) | "yarn" | "yarn" | "wool-threads", "spindles" (ἠλακάτη is distaff or spindle, separately fixed), "thread" |
| κραιπνὰ … προβιβάς (17.27, adverb + participle) | "at a rush … striding forward" | "striding forward at a rush" | "swiftly" (reserved for θοός / ὠκύς), "rushing"; follows the table's κραιπνῶς "at a rush" |
| κακὰ … φύτευεν · κακὰ … φυτεύσω (17.27, 17.82) | "evils … he was planting" · "murder and doom shall plant" | "devising evil" · "sow death and doom" | "plant evils" in `i`, "sowed", "hatched", "slaughter and doom"; 17.27 follows the table row κακὰ δὲ μνηστῆρσι φύτευεν (14.110), 17.82 the shipped φόνον καὶ κῆρα φυτεύει (odyssey-006: "murder and doom … planting", i "sowing death and doom"); `l` keeps the literal "plant" in both places so that the echo can be seen |
| ὣς φάτο (17.26, closing a speech) | "So he spoke" | "So he spoke" | "Thus he spoke", "So he said" |
| ἄπτερος μῦθος (17.57) | "wingless" | "wingless" (+ note: it may mean that she made no answer, which the Greek does not say) | "unwinged", "without effect", "fell flat"; the literal opposite of the shipped ἔπεα πτερόεντα "winged words" |
| ἄντιτα ἔργα (17.51, 17.60) | "deeds of requital" | "deeds of requital" | "vengeance", "revenge", "deeds of retribution", "deeds of recompense"; the word is the adjective ἄντιτος (built on ἀντί and the root of τίνω); whether it means 'requiting' or 'requited' is uncertain, so the rendering stays the neutral "of requital" |
| εὔχεο / εὔχετο … ῥέξειν (17.50, 17.59) | "pray to all the gods, complete hecatombs to offer" | "pray to all the gods, promising to offer complete hecatombs" | "vow", "swear" (the same verb is "pray" at 17.48 in the shipped text); "perform hecatombs"; τεληέσσας keeps the table's "complete" |
| ἀλλ’ ἄγε μοι κατάλεξον ὅπως ἤντησας ὀπωπῆς (17.44) | "But come, recount to me how you came upon the sight." | "But come now, tell me how you came to see it." | "tell me truly" (that is ἐτήτυμον), "tell me exactly" (reserved for ἀτρεκέως κατάλεξον), "set eyes on him" (supplies an object ὀπωπῆς does not have); the `l` and the second half of the `i` are the table row ἀλλ’ εὖ μοι κατάλεξον ὅπως ἤντησας ὀπωπῆς (3.97), the opening is the shipped ἀλλ’ ἄγε μοι … κατάλεξον "But come now, tell me" |
| ἀγορή / ἀγορήνδε (17.52, 17.72) | "the assembly" / "to the assembly" | "the assembly" | "market", "marketplace", "council"; the place of gathering is meant but the word is "assembly" as in the shipped books |
| δουρικλυτός (17.71) | "famed-for-the-spear" | "famed for his spear" | "spear-famed", "famous for his spear", "spear-renowned", "of the glorious spear"; follows the table row δουρικλυτός (15.544) |
| ταλαπείριος (17.84) | "much-tried" | "much tried" | "trial-enduring", "who had endured so many trials", "long-suffering", "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος), "enduring-minded" (reserved for ταλασίφρων); follows the table row ταλαπείριος (7.24) |
| ἔσθλ’ ἀγορεύοντες, κακὰ δὲ φρεσὶ βυσσοδόμευον (17.66, whole line) | "good things speaking, but evils in their minds they were plotting in the depths" | "speaking good things, while in the depths of their minds they plotted evil" | "plotting evil in their hearts", "brooding", "scheming secretly" (each drops βυσσός 'depth'); φρένες stays "mind" |
| πατρώϊοι … ἑταῖροι (17.69) | "his father's own companions" | "companions of his father's day" | "family friends", "hereditary friends"; follows the table's πατρώιος ἑταῖρος row |
| τοὶ δ’ ἐξερέεινον ἕκαστα (17.70) | "and they questioned him about each thing" | "and they asked him about every detail" | "inquired in full", "cross-questioned" |
| τὸν καὶ Πείραιος πρότερος πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε (17.74, speech-introduction; πρὸς … ἔειπε in tmesis) | "Him also Peiraeus, first, with a word addressed:" | "Peiraeus spoke to him first, with these words:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "Him, too, … first to speak spoke to:"; not new: the same line as the table row τὸν καὶ Τηλέμαχος πρότερος πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν (16.460, shipped in odyssey-081), "addressed" being kept in `l` |
| ἐγγύθεν ἦλθεν (17.71) | "from close by came" | "came up from close by" | "from near", "came near", "approached"; follows the shipped "from close by" (odyssey-033, -035, -037) |
| δώσει δέ οἱ ὅς κ’ ἐθέλῃσι (17.11, 17.19) | "and will give him/to me whoever may wish" | "whoever wishes will give him/to me" | "whoever is willing", "anyone who chooses" (both lose the repeated ἐθέλω of the pair) |
| τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε περίφρων Πηνελόπεια (17.100, whole-line speech-introduction) | "and among them of speeches made-beginning circumspect Penelope:" | "circumspect Penelope was the first to speak among them:" | "began the talk", "led the conversation", "wise Penelope"; "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); not new: follows the table row τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε Γερήνιος ἱππότα Νέστωρ and its Athena version (13.374) |
| ὣς εἰπών … ἦγεν ἐς οἶκον (17.84) | "So having spoken … he led to his house." | "So he spoke, and led … to his house." | "With these words" |
| δμῳαί (17.34; 17.88 as shipped) | "maidservants" (17.34) · "slave-women" (17.88) | "maids" (17.34) · "serving-women" (17.88) | "slave-women", "serving-women" at 17.34 (they are the early shipped words for lines that this part repeats, not the table's), "handmaidens" (reserved out); 17.88–89 are 4.49–50, whose shipped English stays word for word; at 17.34 no earlier line binds the wording, so the table row δμῶες / δμῳαί (6.69) applies |
| φάτ’ εἶναι (17.25) | "he said" | "he said" | "it was said", "I am told", "they say", "you said"; φάτ’ is φάτο elided, impf. mid. 3 sg., as the glossary already has it; the note names another parse (φάτε) and says the Greek does not name the speaker |
| στρωφάω (17.97, στρωφῶσα) | "turning" | "twirling" | "spinning", "winding"; follows the shipped "turning yarn" (`l`) and "twirling sea-purple yarn" (`i`, odyssey-029) |
| λάθρη (17.43, 17.80) | "in secret" | "in secret" | "secretly", "stealthily"; follows the table row λάθρη (15.430) |
| ἀγαπαζόμεναι (17.35) | "gladly welcoming" | "welcomed him gladly" | "welcoming warmly", "delighting in"; follows the shipped "gladly welcoming" (odyssey-030) |
| ἀκουήν (17.43, μετὰ πατρὸς ἀκουήν) | "in quest of news of your dear father" | "in search of news of your dear father" | "tidings", "report", "hearing"; follows the table row ἀκουή (14.179) |
